sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Dearborn Heights?
sections.html:
A Dearborn Heights owner can list the house, sell it directly to a buyer, or take a cash offer from an investor who buys as-is. The sale closes with a deed recorded by the Wayne County Register of Deeds, a transfer tax paid at recording, and a few city and assessor steps that Dearborn Heights itself lists for sellers.

A well-kept house can sell through a normal listing. A house with deferred repairs, a deceased owner's estate or a tenant dispute often fits a cash sale better, since the buyer absorbs the condition and the closing timeline is shorter.

  • Listing: widest buyer pool, with inspection and financing contingencies.
  • Direct sale to a buyer: fewer fees, more of the paperwork falls to you.
  • Cash sale: as-is purchase, quicker close, price reflects repairs.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Dearborn Heights as a place?
sections.html:
Dearborn Heights is an inner-ring suburb about 12 miles west of downtown Detroit, packed into under 12 square miles. It was created in 1960 from two separate sections of Dearborn Township joined by a quarter-mile strip of Inkster, which explains its unusual shape. The city counted 63,292 residents in 2020, up 9.6% from the 2010 count.

Water shapes parts of the city. The southern portion lies in the Ecorse Creek watershed, where the area around the creek is subject to flooding, and the north drains toward the Rouge River. The Building Department posts a flood zone map, so check your parcel before you price the house.

A city official put Arab residents at about 25% of the population in 2014, and the Census figures below show how many residents speak another language at home. Marketing in more than one language can widen your buyer pool.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Dearborn Heights houses?
sections.html:
The city is split among five public districts, which makes the exact address matter. North-end residents are usually in Crestwood School District or Dearborn Public Schools, and south-end residents in Westwood Community Schools or the Dearborn Heights School District No. 7. A small part falls within Wayne-Westland Community Schools and Taylor School District.

  • Crestwood High School is on Beech Daly Road.
  • Hamilton Robichaud High School is on Janet Street in Westwood Community Schools.
  • Annapolis High School is on Clippert Street in District No. 7.
  • Dearborn Public Schools residents are zoned to River Oaks, Haigh or Lindberg elementary schools.

Name the district in your listing, because buyers searching by school will filter on it. The city also has two Catholic K-8 schools, St. Anselm and St. Linus, and charter schools including Clara B. Ford Academy.

sections.h2: What does the city ask Dearborn Heights sellers to do?
sections.html:
The city's own page for buyers and sellers sets out a short list. If the house is your primary residence, you must rescind the Principal Residence Exemption when it sells. The title company may hand you the Request to Rescind at closing, and if not, the Assessor's Office at 313-791-3460 can give it to you. This applies even to a quit claim deed with no title company involved.

The same page tells sellers to contact the Building Department at 6045 Fenton (313-791-3470) to learn which inspections the sale requires, since the city offers a residential certificate inspection application. It also tells sellers to contact the Water Department for a final meter reading.

On the buyer's side, a Property Transfer Affidavit must be filed within 45 days of the deed. Late filing carries a fine of up to $200 on a primary residence and up to $4,000 on other residential property.

sections.h2: How much does recording a deed in Wayne County cost?
sections.html:
Wayne County raised its recording fee effective January 1, 2026, the first increase since 1996. A deed now costs $26, plus the $4 state survey and remonumentation fee, for $30 per document regardless of page count.

Transfer tax is paid at the time of recording by cash, check or money order payable to the Wayne County Register of Deeds. The county's rate is $0.55 per $500 and the state's is $3.75 per $500, or $8.60 per $1,000. On a $185,000 sale that comes to $1,591.

Warranty deeds must be certified for payment of property taxes by the Wayne County Treasurer before recording. The deed must state the consideration or cite the exemption statute, and it needs original signatures and a notary acknowledgment. Calling the Register of Deeds at (313) 224-5851 before submission can prevent a rejection.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale the better fit in Dearborn Heights?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits best when the house has problems a retail buyer would not accept, when you must close on a deadline, or when you would rather not run showings. Typical cases include a house needing mechanical work, an inherited property, a landlord ready to exit, and a home with open city inspection items.

Before accepting, ask for the offer in writing, confirm who pays recording and title costs, and check that the buyer will work with the city's rescind and inspection steps. A second quote costs little and shows whether the first is reasonable.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate inspection to sell in Dearborn Heights?
faqs.a: The city directs sellers to its Building Department to find out which inspections apply, and it offers a residential certificate inspection application. Call 313-791-3470 before you list so you know what is required for your address.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax will I pay in Dearborn Heights?
faqs.a: Wayne County lists $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, or $8.60 per $1,000. A $200,000 sale would carry $1,720, due when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Who must file the Property Transfer Affidavit?
faqs.a: The buyer files it with the Assessor's Office within 45 calendar days of the deed. A late filing can carry a fine, so the seller should remind the buyer at closing.

faqs.q: What if I already bought another home before my Dearborn Heights house sold?
faqs.a: Michigan allows only one principal residence exemption, so you must rescind the Dearborn Heights exemption once you move out. The new city may ask for a stamped copy of the rescind form before it grants an exemption on the new home.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Dearborn Heights house in a flood area?
faqs.a: Yes. Parts of the south end sit in the Ecorse Creek watershed where flooding occurs, so check the city's flood zone map and tell your buyer what you know about water in the basement.
